title: Persistent Review lifecycle contract (G0 freeze)
nature: A Review is a persistent, versioned, recoverable, non-authoritative workflow aggregate. It is never a modal popup or an in-memory session. Only the user's committed CanonicalEffect changes canonical research state; the Review itself carries no research authority.
effectDraftAttribute: effect_preview_ready is a persistent attribute of the Review (effect draft, preview hash, base revision), not a second top-level state machine.

creationRule.note: Host and Skill adapters may only create drafts; they never advance the Review.

transitions.note: No Provider is ever required for any effect.

terminalTraceability: Terminal states remain fully traceable: every committed/disposed Review keeps its immutable Receipt, revision event, resulting object references, and correction history readable in History and Search. Terminal states are never deleted or re-opened; corrections and compensations create new work objects that reference the original Review.
recoverySemantics: Each persisted state recovers on restart with no automatic network behavior: running attempts recover as provider_attempt_uncertain; confirmed Manifests never auto-send; effect drafts re-preview after a fresh revision check; commit idempotency is resolved by authorityCommandId lookup against Receipt/resulting object.
correctionSemantics: Corrections are appended Review child records referencing the immutable original assessment. A correction can only end in a typed effect through the same commit path; it never forms a second Resolution truth.
reopenSemantics: Terminal Reviews are never re-opened in place. A user continues work by creating a new Review (optionally sourced from the terminal Review's history); compensation of a committed effect is a new Review/effect, not an edit of the old terminal state.
revisionBinding: The Review stores baseProjectStateRevision. Every commit transaction advances projectStateRevision exactly once and binds Review terminal state, resulting object, revision event, and Receipt in one unit of work.

attemptRules.ordinal: Provider attempts are append-only with strictly increasing ordinals per Review
attemptRules.uncertainty: provider_attempt_uncertain means the request may have been sent; the system never resends automatically and never claims certainty it does not have
attemptRules.manifestBinding: every attempt references exactly one confirmed Manifest identity; retry requires a new Manifest confirmation
